mainTopic: Finishing בית הפרס and the sources for several rules of תמורה: no תמורה from a תמורה or from offspring, and no תמורה for birds, meal offerings, communal offerings, partners, or בדק הבית.
overview: This amud finishes the rule of בית הפרס: a field where a grave was plowed counts for a full furrow, which is 100 אמות. Next, the גמרא shows that the משנה's rule "no תרומה after תרומה" follows רבי עקיבא, based on a dispute about partners who each separated תרומה. It then gives sources in the פסוק for two more rules: a תמורה cannot make another תמורה ("ותמורתו"), and the offspring of a holy animal cannot make a תמורה ("הוא"). רבי יהודה disagrees about the offspring, and the רבנן use his word "יהיה" for a swap made by mistake. A new משנה rules that birds, meal offerings, the community, partners, and בדק הבית items cannot make a תמורה. רבי שמעון learns this by using the animal tithe (מעשר) as the model. The גמרא asks whether בדק הבית items are called "קרבן", and רבי חנינא answers that רבי שמעון and the רבנן disagree. The רבנן tell apart "קרבן ה׳" and "קרבן לה׳". Last, a ברייתא explains why the תורה repeats תמורה by מעשר, and רבי שמעון's list of מעשר's features continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The plowed area covers three fields and two furrows
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its ruling on how far a בית הפרס extends: three fields, with two furrow-lengths.
steps.simpleTranslation: The area counts as three fields and two furrow-lengths.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a statement that began just before this point, about how much land counts as a בית הפרס. A בית הפרס is a field where a grave was plowed up, so bits of bone may be scattered in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plowed field itself is fully a בית הפרס. The two fields next to it, in the direction of the plowing, are included only for a limited stretch: one furrow on each side. This sets up the obvious next question: how long is a furrow?

keyTerms.meaning: A field where a grave was plowed up; it is treated as possibly impure because broken bones may be scattered in it
Fields
Furrows, meaning a plowing-stretch of a set length

phrases.english: Three fields and two furrows.
phrases.notes: This finishes the sentence before it: the two fields next to the plowed one only count for one furrow-length each.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the בית הפרס discussion that started before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בית הפרס covers the plowed field fully, and the two neighboring fields for one furrow-length each.

steps.title: How long is a full furrow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how long a full furrow is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how long is a full furrow?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the measurement of the furrow just mentioned. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling in step 1 depends on the length of a furrow. Without that number, nobody would know how far the impurity reaches into the neighboring fields.

keyTerms.meaning: A full furrow-length
And how much?

phrases.english: And how much is a full furrow?

steps.title: A furrow is one hundred cubits, proven from a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: A furrow is 100 אמות, as a ברייתא about plowing a grave teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: One hundred cubits. As it is taught: one who plows over a grave makes a בית הפרס for a full furrow, which is one hundred cubits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a furrow is 100 אמות long. It backs this up with a teaching about someone who plows over a grave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quoted teaching states directly that plowing a grave creates a בית הפרס "a full furrow, one hundred cubits." So the length is not a guess; it comes from an earlier source.

keyTerms.meaning: Cubit, a measure of roughly an arm's length
One who plows
Grave

phrases.english: One hundred cubits,

makes a בית הפרס

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A מענה is 100 אמות, as the ברייתא about plowing a grave shows.
steps.whatToRemember: A בית הפרס reaches one full furrow, which is 100 אמות.

steps.title: Whose view is the rule of no תרומה after תרומה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next rule of the משנה and asks which תנא it follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And there is no תרומה after תרומה..." Whose opinion is our משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new line in the משנה: once תרומה has been separated, a second separation is not תרומה. It asks which sage holds this view, which sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule sounds simple, but the גמרא knows the sages disagree about it. So it wants to pin the משנה to one specific opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן
Whose view is our משנה?
Etc.; the quote continues in the משנה

phrases.english: "And there is no תרומה after תרומה," etc.
Our משנה, whose view is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a second separation of תרומה is not תרומה.

steps.title: It is רבי עקיבא; the case of partners begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the משנה is רבי עקיבא and starts quoting a משנה about partners who each separated תרומה. רבי אליעזר says both separations count.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי עקיבא, as we learned: partners who separated תרומה one after the other. רבי אליעזר says: the תרומה of both of them is תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that our משנה follows רבי עקיבא. To show this, it begins quoting a dispute about two partners who each separated תרומה from shared produce, starting with רבי אליעזר's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר says both separations are valid, because each partner is seen as separating from his own share. That disagrees with our משנה, so our משנה cannot follow רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: Partners who jointly own produce
Who separated תרומה
One after the other

phrases.english: It is רבי עקיבא,

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: הַשּׁוּתָּפִין שֶׁתָּרְמוּ זֶה אַחַר זֶה,
phrases.english: as we learned: Partners who separated תרומה one after the other,
רבי אליעזר says:
The תרומה of both of them is תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4 and begins quoting the proof.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא and the חכמים on the partners
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says neither separation counts. The חכמים say it depends on whether the first partner gave the right amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: the תרומה of neither of them is תרומה. And the חכמים say: if the first one separated the proper amount, the second one's תרומה is not תרומה. But if he did not separate the proper amount, the second one's תרומה is תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The quote continues with the views of רבי עקיבא and the חכמים. This is the proof that our משנה matches רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא says neither partner's תרומה counts. The חכמים say the second only counts if the first gave too little. Our משנה says flatly "no תרומה after תרומה," with no condition about the amount, so it fits רבי עקיבא and not the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: The proper amount (here, the set measure of תרומה)
The majority of the sages

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up: רבי עקיבא says NEITHER counts, even the first one. Our משנה agrees with him on the main point that the second separation is not תרומה.

phrases.english: רבי עקיבא says:
The תרומה of neither of them is תרומה,
and the חכמים say:
If the first one separated the proper amount,
the תרומה of the second is not תרומה,
and if he did not separate the proper amount,
the תרומה of the second is תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: אֵין תְּרוּמַת שְׁנֵיהֶם תְּרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the quoted source that proves the answer of step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That our משנה (no תרומה after תרומה) follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in תרומות about partners who separated one after the other.
steps.whatToRemember: "No תרומה after תרומה" with no conditions matches רבי עקיבא. The חכמים make it depend on whether the first separation was the proper amount.

steps.title: Why can't a substitute animal make its own substitute?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that a תמורה cannot make a תמורה and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And a תמורה does not make a תמורה..." What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה: an animal that became holy as a substitute cannot pass holiness on to yet another animal. It asks for the source of this rule, which sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, swapping a regular animal for a holy one makes the new animal holy too. The question is why this stops after one round.

keyTerms.meaning: A substitute: an ordinary animal swapped for a holy one, which then becomes holy too
What is the reason / source?

phrases.english: "And a substitute does not make a substitute," etc.
What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source in the תורה for the rule that a תמורה cannot make a תמורה.

steps.title: The פסוק says its substitute, not the substitute of its substitute
steps.stepSummary: The word "ותמורתו" limits the law of substitution to the original holy animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says "and its substitute," and not the substitute of its substitute.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from a פסוק: the תורה says the original animal "and its substitute" are holy. It does not include a substitute made from that substitute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "its" points back to the original holy animal. So the power to make a תמורה belongs only to the first holy animal, not to the animal that became holy through the swap. The substitute is still holy; it just cannot pass its holiness on through another swap.

keyTerms.meaning: "And its substitute"

phrases.english: The verse says: "And its substitute,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:10

phrases.english: and not the substitute of its substitute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word "ותמורתו" limits the law of substitution to the original holy animal.
steps.whatToRemember: A תמורה is holy, but it cannot itself create another תמורה. The source is "ותמורתו," meaning "its substitute," and not the substitute of its substitute.

steps.title: The offspring cannot make a substitute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that the offspring (ולד) of a holy animal cannot make a תמורה. It learns this from the word "הוא" ("it").
steps.simpleTranslation: The offspring does not make a substitute, because the verse says "it": the holy animal itself, and not its offspring.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next rule of the משנה and right away gives its source in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as steps 7–8: a משנה rule, then a word in the פסוק that limits it. The word "הוא" limits תמורה to the holy animal itself. A ולד that became holy only because its mother was holy is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: The offspring born to a holy animal
Swapping a regular animal for a holy one. The regular animal becomes holy too.
Because the verse says

phrases.english: And the offspring does not make a substitute.
For the verse says: "it" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:10

phrases.english: it, and not the offspring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of משנה rules with their sources
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word "הוא" leaves out the ולד

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the offspring can make a substitute
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees and says the ולד can make a תמורה. He learns this from the word "יהיה" ("shall be").
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says the offspring does make a substitute, because the verse says "shall be," which comes to include the offspring.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's view from the משנה and shows which word in the פסוק he uses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה reads the extra word "יהיה" as a ריבוי that adds the ולד. So the two sides are each using a different word in the same פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: To include: an extra word that adds a case
"Shall be": the word in the פסוק that רבי יהודה uses

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
The offspring does make a substitute.
For the verse says "shall be"
to include the offspring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view and its source

steps.title: How the חכמים use the word "shall be"
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים use "יהיה" for a different lesson: a תמורה made by mistake (שוגג) counts like one made on purpose (מזיד).
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן use "shall be" to include someone who swapped by mistake, the same as someone who did it on purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a question it does not say out loud: if the חכמים don't learn the ולד from "יהיה," what do they learn from it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word in the פסוק must teach something. The חכמים agree "יהיה" adds something, but they say it adds the case of שוגג, not the ולד. A swap made without meaning to still takes effect.

keyTerms.meaning: Doing something by mistake, without meaning to
Doing something on purpose

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as the חכמים ignoring "יהיה." They agree it is a ריבוי. They just say it adds the case of שוגג, not the ולד.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis:
phrases.notes: Meaning: and how do the Rabbis use this word?

phrases.english: to include one who acted by mistake, like one who acted on purpose.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the חכמים use רבי יהודה's word
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the word a different use
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the חכמים don't learn the ולד from "יהיה," the word would seem to teach nothing for them
steps.terutzMaskana: For the חכמים, "יהיה" teaches that a swap made by שוגג counts like one made by מזיד
steps.whatToRemember: The ולד: the חכמים say no (from "הוא"), and רבי יהודה says yes (from "יהיה"). For the חכמים, "יהיה" teaches that שוגג counts like מזיד.

steps.title: New משנה: birds and meal offerings cannot make a substitute
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that birds and meal offerings (מנחות) cannot make a תמורה, because the פסוק speaks only about an animal (בהמה).
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Birds and meal offerings do not make a substitute, since the verse speaks only of an animal.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with its first rule: תמורה works only with an animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says "בהמה בבהמה" ("an animal for an animal"). So holy birds and holy flour offerings are left out of the law of תמורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Birds brought as offerings (doves and pigeons)
Meal offerings made of flour
An animal (cattle, sheep, or goats)

phrases.english: Mishna:
The birds and the meal offerings
do not make a substitute,

phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:10

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הָעוֹפוֹת וְהַמְּנָחוֹת אֵין עוֹשִׂין תְּמוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Birds and meal offerings cannot make a תמורה

steps.title: The community and partners cannot make a substitute
steps.stepSummary: An animal owned by the community (ציבור) or by partners (שותפין) cannot make a תמורה. The פסוק speaks in the singular, so only an individual (יחיד) can.
steps.simpleTranslation: The community and partners do not make a substitute, as it says "he shall not exchange it, nor substitute it." An individual makes a substitute, but the community and partners do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second rule, this time about who owns the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "לא יחליפנו ולא ימיר" speak about one person. So the law is limited to a יחיד. Holy animals owned by the community or by partners are left out.

keyTerms.meaning: The community: offerings owned by all of the Jewish people
Partners who own an animal together
An individual owner

phrases.english: The community and the partners

phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:10. The words "he" and "it" are singular. That is the key.

phrases.english: An individual makes a substitute,
but the community and the partners do not make a substitute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next rule in the same משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a יחיד can make a תמורה, not the ציבור or שותפין

steps.title: Items for the Temple's upkeep cannot make a substitute
steps.stepSummary: Items given to בדק הבית (the Temple's upkeep fund) cannot make a תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Items made holy for the upkeep of the Temple do not make a substitute.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a third rule: things given to the Temple fund are not part of תמורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תמורה applies only to animals made holy to be brought on the מזבח. Things given to בדק הבית for their money value are not included.

keyTerms.meaning: Things made holy for the Temple's upkeep fund, not to be offered on the מזבח

phrases.english: Items made holy for the upkeep of the Temple
do not make a substitute.

steps.triggerLanguage: קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת אֵין עוֹשִׂין תְּמוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next rule in the same משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Items given to בדק הבית cannot make a תמורה
steps.whatToRemember: This משנה lists who and what cannot make a תמורה: birds, meal offerings, the ציבור, שותפין, and items given to בדק הבית.

steps.title: רבי שמעון asks why the animal tithe is mentioned separately
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון begins a proof. The animal tithe (מעשר) was already included in the general law of offerings, so why does the תורה mention it on its own?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: The tithe was already included in the general rule. So why was it taken out and mentioned separately?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון asks a question to set up a proof. His answer will come in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule: when a case already inside a general group is singled out, it comes to teach something about the whole group. רבי שמעון is getting ready to use מעשר to learn a rule about who can make a תמורה.

keyTerms.meaning: The animal tithe: every tenth animal of the flock is made holy
It was already included in the general rule
Was taken out and mentioned on its own

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said:
But the tithe was included in the general rule,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי שמעון begins a different source for the rule about the ציבור and שותפין
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the תורה mentions מעשר on its own, even though it was already part of the general law

steps.title: רבי שמעון's answer: compare all offerings to the tithe
steps.stepSummary: מעשר is singled out to teach that only individual offerings and altar offerings make a תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: To teach you: just as מעשר is an individual's offering, community offerings are left out. And just as מעשר is an altar offering, בדק הבית items are left out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון answers his own question from Step 15. The תורה mentions מעשר separately so we can use it as the model for all offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר has two features. It always belongs to one person, and it always goes on the מזבח. Only offerings that share both features can make a תמורה. This gives a source for the rules about the ציבור in Step 13 and about בדק הבית in Step 14.

keyTerms.meaning: The animal tithe, every tenth animal of the herd, which is brought as an offering
An offering that belongs to one individual
Offerings that belong to the whole community
An offering that is brought on the altar
Literally "they went out"; here it means "these are left out"

steps.whatToRemember: מעשר is the model for תמורה. Because it is an individual's offering and an altar offering, community offerings and בדק הבית items do not make a תמורה.

phrases.english: To tell you:

steps.title: A ברייתא: בדק הבית items are not called an offering
steps.stepSummary: The word "קרבן" in the פסוק of תמורה leaves out בדק הבית items, because they are not called "קרבן".
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: You might think בדק הבית items make a תמורה. The פסוק says "קרבן", which means only things called "קרבן". בדק הבית items are left out, because they are not called "קרבן".
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and brings a ברייתא with a different source for the משנה's rule that בדק הבית items cannot make a תמורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source here is the word "קרבן" in the פסוק about תמורה, not the comparison to מעשר. The whole proof depends on one claim: בדק הבית items are never called "קרבן". The next step attacks exactly that claim.

steps.title: Challenge: a ברייתא calls בדק הבית items an offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether בדק הבית items are really not called "קרבן". It quotes a ברייתא that brings a פסוק calling them "קרבן".
steps.simpleTranslation: Are they really not called "קרבן"? But a ברייתא teaches: If the פסוק only said "קרבן", I would include even בדק הבית items, which are called "קרבן", as it says: "And we have brought the offering of ה׳..."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the claim in Step 17. It starts quoting another ברייתא, which says outright that בדק הבית items are called "קרבן".
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in במדבר speaks of jewelry given after the war with מדין, and it calls that gift a "קרבן". So the word "קרבן" can include בדק הבית items. That breaks the reasoning of Step 17.

keyTerms.meaning: "And is it not so?" A sharp question that opens a challenge
"I would understand". It introduces what we would think without a further source
"As it is said". It brings a פסוק as proof

steps.confusionAlert: This second ברייתא is not about תמורה. It is about slaughtering outside the Temple (שחוטי חוץ). The גמרא only uses it to show how the word "קרבן" is used.

phrases.english: And are they not called "offering"?
But isn't it taught in a baraita:
If the verse had said only "offering"
phrases.notes: This ברייתא is reading the פסוק about slaughtering outside the Temple, ויקרא 17:4.

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹמֵעַ אֲנִי אֲפִילּוּ קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת,
phrases.english: I would understand it to include even items consecrated for Temple maintenance,
since they are called "offering",
as it is said:
"And we have brought the offering of the Lord, etc."
phrases.notes: במדבר 31:50. That offering was gold jewelry, not something for the מזבח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim in Step 17 that בדק הבית items are not called "קרבן"
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא in Step 17, which says בדק הבית items are not called "קרבן"
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק in במדבר uses the word "קרבן" for gifts given to בדק הבית

steps.title: The challenge ends: they are called an offering
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא needs a special פסוק to leave בדק הבית items out of שחוטי חוץ. That shows they are normally called "קרבן".
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says "and to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting he did not bring it". Anything that comes to the entrance of the אהל מועד makes one liable for שחוטי חוץ. Anything that does not come there does not make one liable. So we see they are called "קרבן".
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes. The גמרא then states the point of the challenge: בדק הבית items are called "קרבן".
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא had to use a second phrase, "to the entrance of the אהל מועד", to leave out בדק הבית items. That means the word "קרבן" alone would have included them. This directly contradicts Step 17.

keyTerms.meaning: The prohibition of slaughtering an offering outside the Temple area
The entrance of the Tent of Meeting, the place where offerings are brought
One is liable for it
"Evidently". It draws the conclusion from what was just said

phrases.english: Therefore the verse says:
"And to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting he did not bring it"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:4

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַבָּא אֶל פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד
phrases.english: anything that comes to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting
one is liable for it because of slaughtering outside,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל שֶׁאֵינוֹ בָּא לְפֶתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד
phrases.english: and anything that does not come to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting

phrases.aramaic: אֵין חַיָּיבִין עָלָיו מִשּׁוּם שְׁחוּטֵי חוּץ.
phrases.english: one is not liable for it because of slaughtering outside.
Evidently, they are called "offering".

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in Step 18 and draws the conclusion of the challenge
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 17 that בדק הבית items are not called "קרבן"
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A special phrase was needed to leave out בדק הבית items, so the word "קרבן" alone would have included them

steps.title: The two sources follow different opinions
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא says the ברייתא that calls בדק הבית items "קרבן" follows רבי שמעון. The view that they are not called "קרבן" follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: There is no contradiction. One source is רבי שמעון and the other is the רבנן. For רבי שמעון, בדק הבית items are called "offering". For the רבנן, they are not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא answers the challenge from steps 18-19 by splitting the two sources between two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא about שחוטי חוץ assumes בדק הבית items are called "קרבן", and that follows רבי שמעון. That is why רבי שמעון, in the משנה, had to learn the exclusion of בדק הבית from מעשר instead of from the word "קרבן". The רבנן hold they are not called "קרבן", so the word itself leaves them out.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
Is called
The Rabbis, the majority view

steps.whyThisMatters: It explains why רבי שמעון needed his own proof from מעשר (steps 15-16) instead of using the word "קרבן".

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said: It is not difficult.
This one is Rabbi Shimon, that one is the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא about שחוטי חוץ is רבי שמעון. The idea that the word "קרבן" leaves out בדק הבית is the רבנן.

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Shimon, they are called "offering";
according to the Rabbis, they are not called "offering."

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, הָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 18-19
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the sources between two opinions (תנאי היא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed everyone agrees on whether בדק הבית items are called "קרבן"
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון calls them "קרבן"; the רבנן do not

steps.title: A פסוק calls בדק הבית items an offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the רבנן's view with a פסוק that calls בדק הבית gifts "קרבן ה׳".
steps.simpleTranslation: Are they really not called "offering"? But it is written: "And we have brought the Lord's offering"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the רבנן's view by quoting a פסוק where gifts for בדק הבית are called a "קרבן".
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, the army officers brought gold jewelry, which is not an altar offering, and the תורה calls it "קרבן ה׳". So how can the רבנן say בדק הבית items are never called "קרבן"?

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written
The Lord's offering
And is it not so?

phrases.english: And are they not?
But isn't it written: "And we have brought the Lord's offering"!
phrases.notes: במדבר 31:50

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the רבנן's side of רבי חנינא's answer
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's claim that בדק הבית items are not called "קרבן"
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק calls non-altar gifts "קרבן ה׳"

steps.title: "The Lord's offering" is not "an offering to the Lord"
steps.stepSummary: בדק הבית items can be called "קרבן ה׳", but never "קרבן לה׳". The פסוק of תמורה uses the second phrase.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are called "the Lord's offering", but they are not called "an offering to the Lord."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by pointing to a small difference in wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase "קרבן לה׳" is used only for offerings brought on the altar. So when the רבנן say בדק הבית items are not called "קרבן", they mean not with that exact phrase.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering to the Lord, used for altar offerings
An offering brought on the altar
Is not called

steps.confusionAlert: The two phrases look almost the same, but the גמרא treats them as different labels. Only "קרבן לה׳" means an altar offering.

phrases.english: They are called "the Lord's offering,"
they are not called "an offering to the Lord."
phrases.notes: "קרבן לה׳" is the wording used for things brought on the altar, so בדק הבית items don't fit it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 21
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any use of "קרבן" for בדק הבית items proves they are called "קרבן"
steps.terutzMaskana: Only "קרבן לה׳" counts, and that is never used for בדק הבית
steps.whatToRemember: For the רבנן, בדק הבית items can be "קרבן ה׳" but not "קרבן לה׳". That is why the word "קרבן" in the law of תמורה leaves them out.

steps.title: Why does the תורה repeat תמורה for מעשר?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks why the פסוק about מעשר forbids תמורה, when an earlier פסוק already forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: "He shall not inquire whether it is good or bad, neither shall he substitute it". Why is this stated? Wasn't it already stated, "He shall not alter it, nor substitute it, good for bad"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the משנה's rule that communal and partners' offerings don't make a תמורה. It brings a ברייתא that opens with a question, setting up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general פסוק (ויקרא 27:10) already forbids swapping any holy animal. So repeating the ban for מעשר seems extra, and an extra פסוק must be there to teach something.

keyTerms.meaning: Why is it stated? (a sign of an extra פסוק)
Wasn't it already stated?
He shall not inquire (the פסוק about מעשר)
He shall not alter it (the general פסוק of תמורה)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"He shall not inquire whether it is good or bad,
neither shall he substitute it". Why is it stated?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:33

phrases.english: Wasn't it already stated:
"He shall not alter it, nor substitute it,
good for bad, etc."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:10

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section on the משנה's rule about communal offerings
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the extra mention of תמורה by מעשר comes to teach

steps.title: The general פסוק would include every kind of offering
steps.stepSummary: The general פסוק sounds like it covers every offering: individual, communal, altar, and בדק הבית. So the תורה mentions מעשר to narrow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it says "He shall not alter it, nor substitute it," that implies an individual offering, a communal offering, an altar offering, and a בדק הבית offering. Therefore the פסוק says "He shall not inquire."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question. The מעשר פסוק is there to limit how wide the general law of תמורה goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On its own, the general פסוק would apply תמורה to every kind of holy item. Mentioning it again by מעשר, which is an individual altar offering, teaches that only offerings like it make a תמורה. That leaves out communal offerings and בדק הבית, just like the idea in step 16.

keyTerms.meaning: It implies; it sounds like
An offering of one person
An offering of the whole community
Therefore the פסוק says

steps.whatToRemember: The מעשר פסוק limits תמורה to individual altar offerings, so communal offerings do not make a תמורה.

phrases.english: Since it is stated:
"He shall not alter it, nor substitute it,"
it implies an individual offering, a communal offering,
and an altar offering, and a Temple-maintenance offering;
therefore the verse says: "He shall not inquire."
phrases.notes: The idea is that מעשר, the subject of this פסוק, sets the pattern for which offerings make a תמורה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מעשר פסוק narrows the general law so it does not include every type of offering

steps.title: Why was מעשר singled out if it was already included?
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון points out that מעשר was already part of the general rule of תמורה, so its separate mention must be teaching something.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: מעשר was already included in the general group. So why was it taken out and mentioned on its own?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון asks a setup question: why does the תורה mention מעשר separately if the general rule already covered it? This prepares his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a basic rule of learning: when an item that was already inside a general group is pulled out and mentioned on its own, it is there to teach something about the whole group. רבי שמעון is about to use מעשר as a model that defines the general rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, מעשר בהמה: the tenth animal from the herd, which is brought as an offering
It was already included in the general group
So why was it taken out and mentioned on its own?

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said:
But the animal tithe was already in the general category,
phrases.notes: The general category is the earlier פסוק that forbids תמורה for every offering, from Step 23.

phrases.english: so why was it taken out and mentioned separately?

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי מַעֲשֵׂר בַּכְּלָל הָיָה, וְלָמָּה יָצָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the ברייתא's point that the general פסוק seems to cover everything, and starts to explain how the mention of מעשר narrows it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the purpose of mentioning מעשר separately when the general פסוק already included it?

steps.title: מעשר is the model for which offerings can make a תמורה
steps.stepSummary: Just as מעשר is an individual's offering, offered on the altar, brought as an obligation, and not owned in partnership, so too only offerings with these features can create a תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches you: just as מעשר is an individual's offering, an offering for the altar, something brought as an obligation, and something not owned in partnership, so too every offering that makes a תמורה must be an individual's offering, an offering for the altar, and something brought as an obligation...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון answers his own question. מעשר becomes the model, and only offerings that share its features can create a תמורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each feature of מעשר removes a group of offerings. Being a קרבן יחיד removes communal offerings, and being a קרבן מזבח removes בדק הבית gifts, which matches the earlier discussion. Being a חובה and not a partnership adds two more limits. The sentence continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering of one person, not of the whole community
An offering brought on the altar, as opposed to a gift to בדק הבית
Something brought because it is required, not as a voluntary gift
In partnership, owned by several people together
Just as... so too...: a pattern that compares other cases to a model case

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think every offering creates a תמורה. According to רבי שמעון, only offerings that match all the features of מעשר do.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the earlier point that בדק הבית items do not create a תמורה. They fail the 'altar offering' feature that מעשר has.

phrases.english: To tell you:
just as the animal tithe is an individual's offering,
and an offering for the altar,
and something that comes as an obligation,
and something that is not in partnership —
phrases.notes: He means מעשר always belongs to a single owner, never to partners together.

phrases.english: so too, every offering that makes a substitute must be an individual's offering,
and an offering for the altar, and something that comes as an obligation,
phrases.notes: The list isn't finished yet. It continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: לוֹמַר לָךְ: מָה מַעֲשֵׂר קׇרְבַּן יָחִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 25 by using מעשר as a model that limits the general rule.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מעשר is singled out to define the category: only offerings that share its features (individual, altar, obligatory, not in partnership) can create a תמורה.
